title: Define workspace-scoped Mastra signal intake
description: Research and specify how the assistant accepts typed input events through Mastra Signals. Define a validated envelope and map user_prompt, agent/worker responses and progress, CI runs, and other external events to the appropriate Mastra APIs. Clarify workspace-to-resourceId and conversation-to-threadId routing, behavior when a workspace has multiple conversations, per-thread ordering, persistence and crash boundaries, deduplication/coalescing, notification delivery policy, endpoint authentication/webhook verification, and how the assistant reads durable notification payloads. Keep durable worker task lifecycle and side-effect reconciliation in the application task store; Mastra Signals are the thread input/delivery layer, not the task system of record. Verify the design against the installed @mastra/core 1.85.0 API and document any version-specific limitations. Sources: https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/overview, https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/sending-signals, https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/notifications, https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/running-across-processes.
why: Typed user and external events need consistent workspace routing, delivery, ordering, deduplication and recovery rules before implementation.

acceptance.text: Workspace and thread routing is specified, including the multiple-conversations-per-workspace case
Each signal category has a documented mapping to Mastra APIs and payload visibility
Ordering, deduplication, crash recovery, retries and per-workspace writer limits have explicit ownership
Endpoint authentication and external webhook verification are specified
The design is checked against the installed Mastra version and leaves MAST-33 and MAST-34 implementable without overlapping sources of truth

todos.text: Inspect installed Mastra 1.85.0 Signals and notification APIs
Define the normalized event envelope and signal mapping
Document thread routing, ordering, persistence, idempotency and endpoint security
Update MAST-33 and MAST-34 boundaries based on the design

outcome.summary: Specified workspace-scoped intake, event mapping, durable notification and intake-ledger boundaries, routing, ordering, recovery and endpoint security in docs/mastra-signals.md after checking installed @mastra/core 1.85.0 API and official Mastra documentation.
outcome.verifiedBy: Inspected installed declarations/runtime and verified plan via Plantool; MAST-33 task lifecycle and MAST-34 queue/evidence ownership remain distinct from signal intake.
